_meta.source: benchmark/run.py --no-sweep --context (stateless + context) and --no-sweep --agent (agent block), run locally on the corpus as of sulci-oss b25077f. Deterministic: the same command reproduced these values byte-identically on two machines and two Python patch levels before they were written here.
_meta.description: Regression baseline for the built-in TF-IDF engine. These are NOT publishable figures and none of them appears on sulci.io. The site publishes MiniLM numbers (recall 0.9990, false-hit 0.0106, precision 0.9377) measured with --use-sulci across four corpus draws; see sulci-platform/docs/marketing/CLAIMS.md. This file exists to detect UNINTENDED CHANGE in the TF-IDF path, which is what CI runs.
_meta.replaces: The pre-2026-08-07 baseline, which described a corpus that no longer exists: it warmed every group, so every test query had a same-group twin cached, a hit was always available, and the hit rate could only be high. It carried hit_rate 0.8588, false_positive_rate 0.3111, saved_cost_usd 21.47 and the context family 0.816 / 0.776 / 20.8 / 0.176 -- i.e. the retired 85.9%, $21, 81.6%, 77.6%, +20.8pp and +17.6pp site claims, at their source. Those values are deliberately GONE from this file rather than kept for provenance: sulci-oss is public, and a retired figure sitting in a file called baseline.json is found by grep long before anyone reads the note beside it. Their provenance lives in CLAIMS.md and in git history.
_meta.agent_block_note: The agent numbers are UNCHANGED from the previous baseline (0.9497 / 0.43 / 0.9785 / 5 / 31). They never drifted. Every "drift" previously reported against them was a stale agent_summary.json left in benchmark/results/ from a --use-sulci run, compared against these TF-IDF numbers. run.py now stamps _provenance.engine and verify_benchmark.py refuses a mismatch.
_meta.not_checked_by_default: verify_benchmark.py runs `run.py --no-sweep --context` with no --agent, so the agent block is reported as "not measured this run" unless you run `run.py --no-sweep --agent` first. That is expected and is not a failure.
_meta.regeneration_policy: Do NOT refresh this file because it went red. A baseline refreshed whenever it drifts is not a baseline -- it records whatever happened last. Regenerate only when the corpus or the algorithm changes DELIBERATELY, and when you do, update STATUS, regenerated_on, source and replaces in the same commit.
_meta.tolerance_notes: Counts may drift by ±2 across platforms (Linux vs macOS) due to dict-iteration tie-breaks. Headline percentages match exactly. Latency varies by machine; not part of regression check.

stateless._note: total_queries is the TEST set (6,588), not --queries. 2,588 of those rows are should-miss by design (39%), which is why false_positive_rate is high and correct. Read it next to that share, never alone.

context_aware._note: 125 follow-ups across 5 domains. Small. accuracy_delta_pct here is a TF-IDF regression figure and must not be published -- the retired +20.8pp came from this same metric on the old corpus. context_recall / false_hit_rate / precision are recorded for drift detection; verify_benchmark.py does not yet compare them.

agent_workload._note: RETRACTED and not restored: the previous note claimed real-MiniLM gives "~60-75% aggregate vs ~95% TF-IDF". Never measured. Measured 2026-08-04 it gives 95.0%, the same as TF-IDF, which is therefore not an upper bound on this workload. That sentence is where the 60-75% figure in the site hero, the SI pitch deck and the email signature came from.
